BOL1

GeometryCirclesTriangles
Game: Move the dots to change two circles that meet at A and watch their parallel diameters.
How to play: Drag A, O1, O2 or C with a mouse or finger, or focus a dot and use the arrow keys. Press Check the claim to test what you see.
Look for the math

Two circles share the point A. Each has a diameter drawn through it, and the two diameters are parallel. Archimedes claimed that one end of each diameter and the meeting point A always fall on a single line. Drag the dots and see whether that is true.

The claim in the Book of Lemmas

Archimedes' Proposition 1 says: If two circles touch at A, and CD, EF be parallel diameters in them, ADF is a straight line. The applet draws the point C on the small circle, puts D opposite it, then draws the large circle's diameter EF parallel to CD. It keeps E on the same side as C and F opposite. The logic test checks this at 240 tangent circles with many sizes and angles: A, D and F line up every time, and so do A, C and E.

One scaling explains it

When the circles touch, their centres and A lie on one ray. Write the small radius as r, the large one as R, and let u point along the line of centres and v along the two diameters. Then

D = A + r(u − v) and F = A + R(u − v).

Both are the same direction from A, just scaled by R/r. This is a homothety centred at A: it fixes A and carries the small circle onto the large one, so it carries C to E and D to F. The test also checks the longer proof printed on the page: with H on EF and DH parallel to the line of centres, O1H = O2D = O2A and HF = O1O2 = DH, two pairs of isosceles triangles.

Outside and off the line

The page adds that the same proof works when the circles touch from the outside. There the centres lie on opposite sides of A, and the applet's names pair differently: the straight triples are A, C, F and A, D, E, while A, D and F are not on one line. The test checks both pairings. Finally, if you drag O2 away from the line through A and O1, the circles cross instead of touching: the claim's condition is gone and the three points need not line up.

Try Show hint, then drag C all the way around: the two diameters turn together and the straight line through A follows them.
